title: Who pays for active debris removal
bottleneck: Removing one large debris object costs on the order of 86 million euros — ESA's ClearSpace-1 contract price — for a single object, with thousands of high-risk objects in orbit. The operators who created legacy debris often no longer exist; current operators argue they should not subsidize others' junk; governments fund demos but not operational-scale cleanup. It is a textbook tragedy of the commons: everyone benefits from cleaner orbits, nobody wants the bill, and no revenue model closes the gap.
why_it_blocks: Without a payer, removal stays at demo scale while the debris population grows; economics, not technology, is the binding constraint on stabilizing low Earth orbit.
current_state: ESA, JAXA, and startups fly demos; proposals for orbital-use fees and debris credits remain academic. No operational removal market exists.
